title: Structured Reflection — conversational
intro: Hi, I’m Remi. I’m studying how students use AI in their academic work. Think back to the assignments you worked on in CMPM 80H during weeks 3 and 4. Your responses are anonymous and confidential. Ready to begin?
source_instrument: Collaborative AI Metacognition — Ulia structured reflection adaptation

items.prompt: Do you think about what is the most appropriate information to give to the AI?
items.reflection_goal: Learn whether and how the student decides what information to provide to AI.

coverage_targets.description: If the student says yes, explain how they decide what information to give; a bare yes does not cover this.

example_probes: If so, how do you decide what is the most appropriate information to give to the AI?
How do you decide what not to give it?

items.prompt: Do you consider what information the AI needs to perform the task?
items.reflection_goal: Learn whether and how the student considers the information AI needs for a task.

items.prompt: Do you think about what the AI is good and not so good at for the task you’re working on?
items.reflection_goal: Learn whether the student considers AI strengths and limitations, and how that affects their use.
example_probes: If so, how does that influence the way you use AI in your academic work?

items.prompt: Do you think about the best way to divide the work between yourself and the AI?
items.reflection_goal: Learn how the student thinks about dividing work with AI.
example_probes: How do you typically divide it?

items.prompt: Do you review your thinking to ensure that you are not accepting or rejecting the AI’s recommendation too quickly?
items.reflection_goal: Learn whether and how the student reviews their reactions to AI recommendations.

items.prompt: Do you check to make sure the AI is on the right track?
items.reflection_goal: Learn whether and how the student checks AI progress against task goals.
example_probes: If yes, how do you check?

items.prompt: Do you try to ensure that your own mental shortcuts or biases aren’t affecting your reactions to the AI’s output?
items.reflection_goal: Learn whether and how the student checks their own biases when reacting to AI output.
example_probes: If so, how do you check for this?

items.prompt: Do you remind yourself about your own limitations or weaknesses when working with AI on a task?
items.reflection_goal: Learn whether the student considers their own limitations and whether that changes their approach.
example_probes: If so, what limitations or weaknesses do you keep in mind?
How does keeping them in mind change how you approach the task?

items.prompt: Do you think about how you can improve the way you work with AI?
items.reflection_goal: Learn whether and how the student thinks about improving their work with AI.

items.prompt: Do you analyze your thinking before jumping to conclusions regarding the AI’s output?
items.reflection_goal: Learn whether and how the student examines their thinking before drawing conclusions about AI output.

items.prompt: If something goes wrong, do you analyze the situation so you can avoid a similar error in the future?
items.reflection_goal: Learn whether and how the student examines mistakes to avoid repeating them.
